questions.stem: This side view shows the valve situated between the left atrium and left ventricle. How many leaflets does this valve normally have?

explanation.summary: The mitral (bicuspid) valve has two leaflets, an anterior and a posterior leaflet, anchored by chordae tendineae to the papillary muscles. This distinguishes it from the tricuspid, aortic, and pulmonic valves, which each have three cusps.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mitral (bicuspid) valve has two leaflets, an anterior and a posterior leaflet, anchored by chordae tendineae to the papillary muscles. This distinguishes it from the tricuspid, aortic, and pulmonic valves, which each have three cusps.

questions.stem: This side view of the mitral valve labels its leaflets, chordae tendineae, and papillary muscles. During which phase of the cardiac cycle do these leaflets normally open to allow flow?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continuously throughout the entire cardiac cycle

explanation.summary: The mitral valve opens during diastole to permit blood to flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle, and closes during systole to prevent backflow. The chordae tendineae and papillary muscles tether the leaflets to prevent prolapse.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mitral valve opens during diastole to permit blood to flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle, and closes during systole to prevent backflow. The chordae tendineae and papillary muscles tether the leaflets to prevent prolapse.

questions.stem: This diagram depicts a catheter-based treatment for mitral stenosis. How does inflating the balloon at the valve relieve the obstruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It replaces the diseased leaflets with a prosthetic disc

choices.label: B
choices.text: It removes calcium deposits by mechanical abrasion of the annulus

choices.label: C
choices.text: It ablates the abnormal electrical pathways in the atrium

choices.label: D
choices.text: It shrinks a dilated annulus back to normal diameter

choices.label: E
choices.text: It splits the fused commissures, widening the valve orifice

explanation.summary: Percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy advances a catheter via a transseptal puncture to the mitral valve, where balloon inflation splits the fused commissures and enlarges the stenotic orifice.
explanation.whyCorrect: Percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy advances a catheter via a transseptal puncture to the mitral valve, where balloon inflation splits the fused commissures and enlarges the stenotic orifice.
